questions.question: According to the scenario described for the KidsTakePics system, what primary role does the teacher play in the photo‑upload process?

options.B: Moderates the uploaded photos to ensure suitability for sharing.
options.C: Compresses the photos to reduce file size.
options.D: Sends notifications to students when uploads complete.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: In the detailed scenario description for iLearn, why are scenarios preferred over simple stories when discussing requirements with stakeholders?

options.B: Scenarios are shorter and require less time to read.
options.C: Scenarios can illustrate multiple ways to achieve the same result, facilitating stakeholder discussion.
options.D: Scenarios eliminate the need for a requirements document.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The text notes that scenarios can be used to facilitate discussions with stakeholders who may have different ways of achieving the same result. [Page 19]

questions.question: When specifying requirements, which characteristic is described as “almost impossible to achieve” in practice?

options.A: Having requirements that are clear, unambiguous, easy to understand, complete, and consistent.
options.B: Ensuring all requirements are written in a programming language.
options.C: Guaranteeing that every requirement can be verified with automated tests.
options.D: Limiting the number of requirements to fewer than ten.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The text states that ideally requirements should be clear, unambiguous, easy to understand, complete, and consistent, but achieving all of these is almost impossible. [Page 20]
